items.followUp: Name two devices that convert solar energy into useful forms, and state the form of energy produced by each.

rubric.why: Defines solar energy.
rubric.description: Defines solar energy as energy obtained from the Sun.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the Sun as its source.

rubric.why: Identifies conversion of solar energy into electrical energy.
rubric.description: States that solar cells or panels convert sunlight into electrical energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the device and resulting form of energy.

rubric.why: Identifies conversion of solar energy into heat.
rubric.description: Gives a solar cooker or heater as a means of obtaining useful heat.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a suitable device and the heat produced.

rubric.why: Explains how sunlight is made useful in an application.
rubric.description: Explains that sunlight falling on a solar device provides electricity or useful heating.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for connecting the incoming sunlight to a useful output.

modelAnswer: Solar energy is the energy received from the Sun in the form of light and heat.
Solar cells convert sunlight directly into electrical energy.
Solar cookers and solar water heaters absorb sunlight and convert it into heat for cooking or heating water.
Thus, solar energy can be converted into useful electrical and thermal forms.

items.followUp: A spanner 25 cm long is used with a force of 80 N to turn a nut. What force applied at a distance of 40 cm from the nut will produce the same turning effect?

rubric.why: Identifies the given forces and converts the first spanner length to SI units.
rubric.description: Writes the given data in SI units: 200 N, 0.10 m, and 150 N.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly recording the data, including the length conversion.

rubric.why: Uses the relation between moment and force.
rubric.description: States moment (turning effect) = force × perpendicular distance.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct relation.

rubric.why: Calculates the moment needed to loosen the nut.
rubric.description: Finds the required moment as 20 N m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct initial moment calculation with units.

rubric.why: Sets the moment produced by the 150 N force equal to the required moment.
rubric.description: Uses 150 N × required length = 20 N m.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly equating the moments.

rubric.why: Gives the required spanner length.
rubric.description: Obtains approximately 0.133 m, or 13.3 cm.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct length with a suitable unit.

modelAnswer: Given: F₁ = 200 N, r₁ = 10 cm = 0.10 m, F₂ = 150 N.
Required: r₂.
Formula: Moment = force × perpendicular distance.
For the same nut, the moments are equal: F₁r₁ = F₂r₂.
Substitution: (200 N)(0.10 m) = (150 N)r₂.
Answer: The required spanner length is approximately 0.133 m (13.3 cm).

items.followUp: What is physics? Name two main branches of physics.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of physics.
rubric.description: Defines physics as the branch of science concerned with matter, energy, and their relationship or interaction.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning matter and energy and how they are related.

rubric.why: Checks both branches.
rubric.description: Names classical physics and modern physics.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both branches.

modelAnswer: Physics is the branch of science that deals with the study of matter, energy, and the relationship between them.
Its two main branches are classical physics and modern physics.

items.followUp: Write the number 0.000072 in scientific notation.

rubric.why: Checks that scientific notation is expressed as a product involving a power of ten.
rubric.description: States that a number is written as a product of a number and a power of 10.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the product form and power of ten.

rubric.why: Checks the required range of the coefficient.
rubric.description: States that the numerical coefficient is at least 1 and less than 10.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving the coefficient range.

modelAnswer: Scientific notation is a way of expressing a number as the product of a number between 1 and 10 and a power of 10.

items.followUp: Define a physical quantity and give two examples other than length and mass.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of a physical quantity.
rubric.description: States that a physical quantity can be measured.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it is measurable.

rubric.why: Checks for examples of physical quantities.
rubric.description: Gives two valid examples, such as length and mass or time and temperature.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for two correct examples.

modelAnswer: A physical quantity is a property that can be measured and expressed by a numerical value and a unit.
Examples include length and mass.

items.followUp: Define speed and write its equation.

rubric.why: Checks the definition of velocity.
rubric.description: Defines velocity as the rate of change of displacement with time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for relating displacement to time.

rubric.why: Checks the equation for velocity.
rubric.description: Writes velocity = displacement ÷ time.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct equation.

modelAnswer: Velocity is the rate of change of displacement with time.
Equation: v = displacement ÷ time, or v = s/t.

items.followUp: Describe one difference between translatory motion and rotatory motion.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of rotatory motion.
rubric.description: States that rotatory motion is motion about a fixed axis.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying rotation about an axis.

rubric.why: Checks the defining feature of vibratory motion.
rubric.description: States that vibratory motion is repeated to-and-fro motion about a mean position.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing oscillation about the mean position.

modelAnswer: In rotatory motion, a body moves around a fixed axis.
In vibratory motion, a body moves repeatedly to and fro about its mean position.

items.followUp: Define sliding friction and state when it acts.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of rolling friction.
rubric.description: States that rolling friction opposes motion when a body rolls over a surface.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking rolling motion over a surface with its opposing friction.

rubric.why: Checks the meaning of sliding friction.
rubric.description: States that sliding friction opposes motion when one surface slides over another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for linking sliding surfaces with their opposing friction.

modelAnswer: Rolling friction is the frictional force that opposes the motion of a body rolling over a surface.
Sliding friction is the frictional force that opposes motion when one surface slides over another.
